finding: Tanh-bounded adaptive transport exhibits robust hysteresis-like memory.
interpretation: Path-dependent adaptive transport remains after replacing hard clipping with smooth tanh bounds.

finding: Topology-only memory forms a distinct memory class.
interpretation: Transport output can converge while coupling topology retains history.
The topology-only memory result is not only a loose-threshold artifact.

finding: Coupled transport-topology memory is the dominant memory class.
interpretation: Many cases retain both observable transport memory and structural topology memory.

finding: Persistent topology-only memory survives lifetime testing.
interpretation: Selected topology-only cases preserve structural memory after transport-output convergence.

finding: Spectral topology memory remains nearly unchanged during lifetime hold.
interpretation: Relative structural memory persists even while absolute spectral strength relaxes.
Topology memory is basin-supported, not merely frozen or perfectly invariant.

finding: Pure topology-only survival persists under perturbation in a substantial subset.
interpretation: The topology-only memory phase is robust under state and coupling perturbations.

finding: Memory erasure exists as a competing basin outcome.
interpretation: Perturbations can erase memory, indicating basin erosion rather than absolute freezing.

finding: Memory retention remains partially preserved across perturbation space.
interpretation: The robustness landscape supports graded memory survival.
